FFLA marks the Leesburg tower as gone
Community of the same name lies seven miles west of Pittsburg in western Camp County, on the Louisiana and Arkansas Railway and State Highway 11
evidence.quote: Leesburg is on the Louisiana and Arkansas Railway and State Highway 11, seven miles west of Pittsburg in western Camp County.

evidence.supports: Community named for the John Lee family, early settlers in the area
evidence.quote: It was named for the John Lee family, early settlers in the area.

evidence.supports: Community was one of three towns proposed as county seat in 1874 and finished second to Pittsburg
evidence.quote: In 1874 Leesburg was one of three towns proposed to be the county seat of Camp County; it finished second to Pittsburg.

evidence.supports: Post office called Leesburgh established in 1874
evidence.quote: That year a post office called Leesburgh was established with James G. Credille, the county treasurer, as postmaster.
The spelling was changed to Leesburg around 1900.

sources.title: Texas Lookouts, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Thin. The only tower-specific source is the FFLA Texas list, which gives name, county, coordinates and gone status and nothing else. Not on NHLR or FFLOS. Two searches and a handful of page reads found no build date, design, staffing, fires or site description. The TSHA material describes the town, not the tower; the link between the tower and the community rests on the shared name, which no source states. The Rootsweb Camp County page returned 403 and was not read. Coordinates were not checked against a map. The editor may cut the community paragraph if it reads as padding.
